Spec 09 Better Graphics (#35) — semantic diff

Branch feature/better-graphicsBase 91cc8be (main before the branch)Head 060ff79 Target mainDate 2026-11-22 Commits 22Files 491 · +23793 / −706 (ProtonScatter 4.2.0: 334 files, +16,152) Written by REVIEW: + CODE REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

Spec 09 gives the Godot game the outlined cartoon look of the Python + Svelte game, adds a second world built with ProtonScatter, turns Mattia's drawing into a fighter and recommends a drawing-to-3D workflow. Range 91cc8be..060ff79: the requirements and plan commits and Steps 1–20 (Step 19, the author's Google Flow/Meshy trial, is deferred).

  • Every menu screen stands on a purple gradient with light rays; the logo, headings, buttons and numbers use Lilita One with a dark outline; home has coloured icon buttons and a big yellow Play; trophies, credits, power, timer and fighters left are icon chips; fighter cards and skin buttons show pictures in rarity colours.
  • Fighters, the canyon and the new props share one cel shader with three bands and a screen-space outline; the camera keeps the near wall to at most 8 % of the screen; the FPS label is hidden unless Info's Show FPS (play-test) is on.
  • Glimmer Isles (same size and rules as the canyon) is chosen on home for Play and Training; its props are placed with ProtonScatter and baked, so no addon code or thread runs in the game; the addon is pinned, credited and excluded from the export.
  • Beatbolt, built from shapes after Mattia's drawing, is a seventh fighter unlocked for every save; the workflow and tool documents say how to add or remove one.
  • 468 of 468 tests pass, lint and check_tools.ps1 are clean, the web export grows by 0.16 MB (budget 5 MB); server/ and ui/ are unchanged. Ten findings, none Blocking: the architecture's test list misses the five look tests, and G11 is tested only in the canyon.

Recommendation: Approve with follow-ups — no Blocking finding; findings 1–7 to fix now, 8–9 deferred, 10 a plan decision. Accepted as deferred (not findings): the G1 verdict, Mattia's A3 confirmation, the iPad G14/W5 play-test and the B6 trial (Step 19).

Semantic diff

Why: The author and Mattia found the Godot game's screens and characters much worse than the Python + Svelte game (flat navy screens, default font, five identical purple buttons, a thin outline, a yellow checker floor with a wall over a quarter of the match). Spec 09 gives every screen and fighter an outlined cartoon look like the Svelte game, adds a second world (Glimmer Isles, placed with ProtonScatter and baked), turns Mattia's drawing into a fighter (Beatbolt) and recommends a drawing-to-3D workflow.

Breaking: none for players and saves: version 3 saves load (an old save gets Beatbolt unlocked), the server and the Python + Svelte game are unchanged. For code: Hacks.credits_text was renamed Hacks.credits_amount (no other caller), and the HUD and card labels became IconChips (node paths TimerLabel, FightersLeftLabel, TrophiesLabel, PowerLabel, LockLabel are gone). · Checks: 6 pass · 2 n/a · 1 fail

Author Q&A

Why is ProtonScatter's result baked instead of running in the game?
D12/W5: ProtonScatter rebuilds on a Thread at load, which the single-threaded web export cannot rely on and which costs start-up time. tools/bake_world.ps1 rebuilds it on the main thread once and saves plain MultiMeshInstance3D nodes; the game never loads addon code (test_glimmer_isles.gd checks baked.tscn has no addon path), and the addon is excluded from the export.
Why a screen-space inverted hull instead of Godot's grow outline?
D5/G9: the old 0.022 m grow vanished at card size. outline.gdshader grows each vertex out from the part's centre by 0.012 m and then by 3 px on screen (scaled above 720 px), so the outline reads on a 150 px card and in the arena. It costs one extra pass per outlined mesh (Training 384 -> 539 draw calls on the desktop, Step 5); the iPad check is deferred.
How does the arena pick its world without changing Arena's logic?
D9: ArenaLayout.use(GameState.world) swaps the active layout (static variables) and the functions and accessors read it; Arena handles NOTIFICATION_SCENE_INSTANTIATED to replace its Canyon node with GlimmerIsles before any child is ready. The canyon constants are unchanged (W7).
How is a drawn fighter added or removed?
D14/A9: a look file scenes/drawn/<id>_model.gd, a row in DrawnFighters.MODELS, an entry in Fighters.LIST ("drawn": true, "plays_like") and two SampleProgress numbers. A save that chose a removed fighter falls back to Blaze (test_drawn_fighter.gd); docs/drawing_to_fighter.md.

Highlights

1 · The world is chosen before the arena's children are ready

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.gd:75-97 · f5eda37 · Step 11 · W2, W4, D9

75func _notification(what: int) -> void:
76 # Before any child is ready: the chosen world's layout and scenery (spec 09, D9).
77 if what == NOTIFICATION_SCENE_INSTANTIATED:
78 _use_world()
79
80
81## Makes the chosen world (`GameState.world`) the active layout and, for Glimmer Isles, puts
82## `GlimmerIsles` in place of the scene's `Canyon`, on the same floor and walls.
83func _use_world() -> void:
84 ArenaLayout.use(GameState.world)
85 # An inherited scene (`match.tscn`) gets the notification once per scene level.
86 if ArenaLayout.world() == Worlds.CANYON or not has_node("Canyon"):
87 return
88 var canyon: Node = get_node("Canyon")
89 var isles: GlimmerIsles = GlimmerIsles.new()
90 isles.name = "GlimmerIsles"
91 isles.floor_body = get_node("Floor")
92 isles.walls = get_node("Walls")
93 add_child(isles)
94 move_child(isles, canyon.get_index())
95 remove_child(canyon)
96 canyon.free()
97

What changed: Arena handles NOTIFICATION_SCENE_INSTANTIATED: it makes GameState.world the active ArenaLayout and, for Glimmer Isles, swaps the scene's Canyon node for a GlimmerIsles node on the same Floor and Walls before any _ready runs.

Why it matters: The arena keeps one scene for both worlds and match.tscn (which inherits it) needs no change; dummies, starts and the bots then read the active layout.

What to check: That the inherited scene does not replace twice (the has_node("Canyon") guard) and that the canyon path is untouched (W7). The active layout stays set after the arena closes (finding 7).

Concepts: NOTIFICATION_SCENE_INSTANTIATEDSent to a scene's root right after PackedScene.instantiate() built the tree, before it enters the scene tree; here it lets the root swap a child before any child's _ready. move_childPuts a node at a given index among its siblings; GlimmerIsles takes Canyon's place so the node order (and so the draw and ready order) stays the same. free()Deletes a node at once (not at the end of the frame like queue_free); safe here because the Canyon node is outside the tree and nothing references it.

2 · The camera never looks past the near wall

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.gd:287-323 · 4ff01cd · Step 6 · G11

287
288
289## Moves the camera back until the box around the fighter fits the screen, so it works in
243## landscape and portrait.
290## landscape and portrait; then finds how far south the camera may look.
291func _frame_camera() -> void:
292 var view_size: Vector2 = get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size
293 var allowed: Rect2 = Rect2(
294 view_size * Vector2(FRAME_MARGIN, FRAME_TOP_MARGIN),
297 _camera_distance = CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE
298 while _camera_distance < CAMERA_MAX_DISTANCE:
299 _place_camera()
300 if _box_inside(allowed):
254 return
301 break
302 _camera_distance += CAMERA_DISTANCE_STEP
303 _camera_max_z = near_wall_z() - _near_wall_offset(view_size.y)
304 _place_camera()
305
306
307# How far south of the camera target the near wall's top edge may be, so that the wall covers
308# at most `NEAR_WALL_SHARE` of the screen height. The camera moves with its target, so the answer
309# does not depend on where the target is.
310func _near_wall_offset(view_height: float) -> float:
311 var wall_top: float = Canyon.CAMERA_SIDE_WALL_HEIGHT + WALL_CAP_HEIGHT
312 var wanted_y: float = view_height * (1.0 - NEAR_WALL_SHARE)
313 var near: float = 0.0
314 # Not past the camera itself, where a point would be behind it.
315 var far: float = _camera_distance * cos(deg_to_rad(CAMERA_PITCH_DEGREES))
316 for _step: int in 40:
317 var offset: float = (near + far) / 2.0
318 var edge: Vector3 = _camera_target + Vector3(0.0, wall_top, offset)
319 if _camera.unproject_position(edge).y < wanted_y:
320 near = offset
321 else:
322 far = offset
323 return near

What changed: After the distance is found, _near_wall_offset bisects how far south of the camera target the near wall's top edge may lie so it projects at 92 % of the screen height, and the camera target is clamped (_camera_max_z).

Why it matters: G11: the near wall covered 26-43 % of the screen at the start; now at most 8 % at the five sizes, with no wall height changed (W7).

What to check: The bisection bound (never behind the camera), that the limit is recomputed on size_changed, and that both worlds use the same wall height (only the canyon is tested, finding 2).

Concepts: Camera3D.unproject_positionReturns the 2D screen position of a 3D point for this camera; the test and the bisection use it to measure where the wall's top edge lands on screen. bisectionHalves an interval 40 times to find the largest offset whose projection stays above the wanted line; the projection grows monotonically with the offset, so it converges. size_changedViewport signal when the window or sub-viewport changes size; the framing is computed again so a rotated phone gets its own limit.

4 · The outline that keeps its width on screen

hack_star_godot/scenes/toon/outline.gdshader:1-28 · 9d0d868 · Step 3 · G9, D5

1shader_type spatial;
2render_mode unshaded, cull_front, shadows_disabled;
3// The dark outline (spec 09, D5): an inverted hull, drawn as the toon material's next pass. Each
4// vertex moves out from the part's centre by `grow` metres (thick on close-ups, as the Svelte
5// game's hull) and then by `width_px` pixels on screen (3 px while the shorter side of the view is
6// up to 720 px, more on bigger screens), so the outline stays visible on a card and on a small
7// fighter in the arena.
8
9uniform vec4 outline_color : source_color = vec4(0.086, 0.059, 0.2, 1.0);
10uniform float width_px = 3.0;
11uniform float grow = 0.012;
12
13void vertex() {
14 // Out from the centre, not along the face normal: box corners stay closed.
15 vec3 out_dir = length(VERTEX) > 0.0001 ? normalize(VERTEX) : NORMAL;
16 vec4 clip = PROJECTION_MATRIX * (MODELVIEW_MATRIX * vec4(VERTEX + out_dir * grow, 1.0));
17 vec3 view_dir = (MODELVIEW_MATRIX * vec4(out_dir, 0.0)).xyz;
18 vec2 screen_dir = (PROJECTION_MATRIX * vec4(view_dir, 0.0)).xy;
19 if (length(screen_dir) > 0.0001) {
20 float pixels = width_px * max(1.0, min(VIEWPORT_SIZE.x, VIEWPORT_SIZE.y) / 720.0);
21 clip.xy += normalize(screen_dir) * pixels * 2.0 / VIEWPORT_SIZE * clip.w;
22 }
23 POSITION = clip;
24}
25
26void fragment() {
27 ALBEDO = outline_color.rgb;
28}

What changed: An inverted hull drawn as the toon material's next pass: each vertex moves out from the part's centre by 0.012 m and then by 3 px in clip space (more above 720 px).

Why it matters: G9: the old 0.022 m grow vanished at card size; a pixel width reads on a 150 px card and in the arena alike.

What to check: Box corners stay closed (out from the centre, not the face normal); the cost is one more draw per outlined mesh (Step 5: 384 -> 539 draw calls in Training on the desktop); the iPad check is deferred.

Concepts: next_passA material drawn again after the first pass on the same mesh; the outline is the second pass of every toon material. cull_frontDraws only the back faces; the grown back faces show as a dark rim around the front faces - the inverted hull technique. clip spaceCoordinates after the projection matrix, before the divide by w; adding pixels * 2 / VIEWPORT_SIZE * w moves a vertex by a fixed number of pixels.

5 · Three bands of light

hack_star_godot/scenes/toon/toon.gdshader:17-33 · 9d0d868 · Step 3 · G9, G10

17void fragment() {
18 ALBEDO = use_instance_color ? albedo.rgb * COLOR.rgb : albedo.rgb;
19 ROUGHNESS = 1.0;
20 SPECULAR = 0.0;
21 EMISSION = emission.rgb * emission_energy;
22}
23
24void light() {
25 float facing = dot(NORMAL, LIGHT);
26 // A surface in a cast shadow gets the shadow band, whatever it faces.
27 float lit = ATTENUATION > 0.5 ? facing : -1.0;
28 float band = mix(shadow_band, mid_band, smoothstep(-0.12, -0.04, lit));
29 band = mix(band, lit_band, smoothstep(0.36, 0.44, lit));
30 DIFFUSE_LIGHT += LIGHT_COLOR * band / PI;
31 float rim = smoothstep(0.66, 0.72, 1.0 - dot(NORMAL, VIEW)) * smoothstep(0.1, 0.3, lit);
32 SPECULAR_LIGHT += LIGHT_COLOR * rim * rim_strength / PI;
33}

What changed: fragment() sets the albedo (tinted per MultiMesh instance when use_instance_color is on); light() turns each light into a lit, a mid and a shadow band with smoothsteps, and adds a thin rim.

Why it matters: G9's 'at least two clear tones per colour' and the Svelte game's 3-step look, also on the canyon and world props.

What to check: The band edges and that a cast shadow forces the shadow band; works in the Compatibility renderer.

Concepts: light()A spatial shader function run per light per pixel; whatever it adds to DIFFUSE_LIGHT replaces Godot's default diffuse, which allows banded (cel) shading. smoothstep0 below the first edge, 1 above the second, smooth between; narrow edges give crisp but not aliased bands. ATTENUATIONThe light's shadow and distance factor at the pixel; below 0.5 the pixel is treated as in shadow.

6 · A see-through copy for a fighter in a bush

hack_star_godot/scenes/toon/toon_materials.gd:72-111 · 9d0d868 · Step 3 · G9, A4

72## A see-through copy of a material for a fighter in a bush. Writing ALPHA in the toon shader
73## would make every part transparent all the time (sorting, cost), so the copy is a plain
74## transparent toon `StandardMaterial3D` with a faded outline. Other materials are faded too.
75static func see_through(material: Material) -> Material:
76 if material == null:
77 return null
78 if not _see_through.has(material):
79 _see_through[material] = _faded(material)
80 return _see_through[material]
81
82
83static func _faded(material: Material) -> Material:
84 if is_toon(material):
85 var source: ShaderMaterial = material
86 var copy: StandardMaterial3D = StandardMaterial3D.new()
87 var color: Color = source.get_shader_parameter("albedo")
88 copy.albedo_color = Color(color, SEE_THROUGH_ALPHA)
89 copy.diffuse_mode = BaseMaterial3D.DIFFUSE_TOON
90 copy.specular_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SPECULAR_DISABLED
91 copy.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
92 var energy: float = source.get_shader_parameter("emission_energy")
93 if energy > 0.0:
94 copy.emission_enabled = true
95 copy.emission = source.get_shader_parameter("emission")
96 copy.emission_energy_multiplier = energy
97 if source.next_pass != null:
98 copy.next_pass = see_through(source.next_pass)
99 return copy
100 if material == _outline:
101 var faded_outline: StandardMaterial3D = StandardMaterial3D.new()
102 faded_outline.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
103 faded_outline.albedo_color = Color(OUTLINE_COLOR, SEE_THROUGH_ALPHA)
104 faded_outline.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
105 faded_outline.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_FRONT
106 faded_outline.grow = true
107 faded_outline.grow_amount = SEE_THROUGH_OUTLINE_GROW
108 return faded_outline
109 if material is StandardMaterial3D:
110 var plain: StandardMaterial3D = material.duplicate() as StandardMaterial3D
111 plain.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA

What changed: ToonMaterials.see_through caches one transparent StandardMaterial3D per toon material, with a faded grown outline as its next pass.

Why it matters: Keeps the see-through of spec 06 working without making every toon material transparent all the time (sorting and cost).

What to check: The copy is cached per material; the outline copy uses Godot's grow because the screen-space outline needs an opaque pass.

Concepts: TRANSPARENCY_ALPHADraws the material in the transparent pass, sorted back to front, so the fighter shows through the cactus or fern patch. material_overrideA material on the GeometryInstance3D that replaces the mesh's surface materials; the see-through swap changes only this property.

What to check: The metadata is written by the bake tool because a headless MultiMesh holds no transforms; test_glimmer_isles.gd checks that every MultiMesh is filled.

Concepts: MultiMeshDraws many copies of one mesh in one draw call with a transform (and optional colour) per instance; one per prop part keeps each part's outline. set_meta / get_metaArbitrary values stored on an Object and saved in the scene; here the places and colours of each baked part.

8 · The bake reads ProtonScatter's places

hack_star_godot/tools/bake_world.gd:71-92 · 96a4ffd · Step 13 · W5, D12

71# Every place of every item of `scatter`, relative to the source scene's root, by prop kind (the
72# item's scene file name). Read from the scatter's transform list and split between its items as
73# ProtonScatter does for its MultiMeshes (`_update_multimeshes`, chunks off): the output's own
74# MultiMeshes hold no transforms without a renderer.
75func _collect(source: Node3D, scatter: Node3D, places: Dictionary[String, Array]) -> void:
76 var base: Transform3D = source.global_transform.affine_inverse() * scatter.global_transform
77 var list: Array = scatter.get("transforms").get("list")
78 var total: int = scatter.get("total_item_proportion")
79 var offset: int = 0
80 for item: Node in scatter.get("items"):
81 var kind: String = String(item.get("path")).get_file().get_basename()
82 if not places.has(kind):
83 places[kind] = []
84 var count: int = roundi(float(item.get("proportion")) / total * list.size())
85 for index: int in count:
86 if offset + index >= list.size():
87 break
88 var place: Transform3D = item.call("process_transform", list[offset + index])
89 places[kind].append(base * place)
90 offset += count
91
92

What changed: _collect reads each scatter's transform list and splits it between its items by proportion, the way ProtonScatter fills its own MultiMeshes, then applies each item's process_transform.

Why it matters: Makes the bake work headless (no renderer) and deterministic: a re-bake in this review gave the same baked.tscn except Godot's random unique_ids.

What to check: The roundi split must match ProtonScatter 4.2.0's own; a ProtonScatter upgrade needs a re-check. tools/*.gd is not linted (finding 8).

Concepts: SceneTree script (-s)godot -s runs a script that extends SceneTree as the main loop; the bake uses it to load a scene, wait frames and save without the editor. PackedScene.packTurns a node tree (nodes owned by the root) into a scene resource that ResourceSaver.save writes as .tscn.

Code review (CODE REVIEW:) of 91cc8be..060ff79, layer by layer (spec, architecture, code, quick scan). Ran: tools/check_tools.ps1 (exit 0, ProtonScatter 4.2.0), tools/lint.ps1 (exit 0), tools/test.ps1 (468 of 468 passed), tools/export_web.ps1 (exit 0); tools/bake_world.ps1 re-run in a clean worktree (same baked.tscn but Godot's random unique_ids); record checked with change_record.schema.json; a headless probe and windowed screenshots on both sides. Good: every Step checked its look on real screenshots and wrote what it changed after looking; one shared material cache for fighters, canyon and props; the ProtonScatter thread risk is removed by baking, with a test that the baked scene has no addon reference; the arena framing is a measured rule with a test that fails on the old framing; the drawn-fighter tests are generic, so adding or removing a drawing touches no test; the author's untracked work was kept out of the commits and the size was measured without it; deviations (no price on cards, the world button's place, the see-through copy, the bake reading transforms) are written in the Notes.

Godot packs every resource of the folder: a working-tree export is 45,232,931 bytes (+4.87 MB against the baseline instead of +0.16 MB), so committing them later would use almost all of G15's 5 MB.

Concepts glossary

NOTIFICATION_SCENE_INSTANTIATED
Sent to a scene's root right after PackedScene.instantiate() built the tree, before it enters the scene tree; here it lets the root swap a child before any child's _ready.
move_child
Puts a node at a given index among its siblings; GlimmerIsles takes Canyon's place so the node order (and so the draw and ready order) stays the same.
free()
Deletes a node at once (not at the end of the frame like queue_free); safe here because the Canyon node is outside the tree and nothing references it.
Camera3D.unproject_position
Returns the 2D screen position of a 3D point for this camera; the test and the bisection use it to measure where the wall's top edge lands on screen.
bisection
Halves an interval 40 times to find the largest offset whose projection stays above the wanted line; the projection grows monotonically with the offset, so it converges.
size_changed
Viewport signal when the window or sub-viewport changes size; the framing is computed again so a rotated phone gets its own limit.
static var
A script-level variable shared by every use of the class (GDScript 2.0); here the active layout, so static functions can read it without an instance.
const Array[Rect2]
A typed constant array is read-only at run time, so handing it out from walls() cannot let a caller change a world's layout.
next_pass
A material drawn again after the first pass on the same mesh; the outline is the second pass of every toon material.
cull_front
Draws only the back faces; the grown back faces show as a dark rim around the front faces - the inverted hull technique.
clip space
Coordinates after the projection matrix, before the divide by w; adding pixels * 2 / VIEWPORT_SIZE * w moves a vertex by a fixed number of pixels.
light()
A spatial shader function run per light per pixel; whatever it adds to DIFFUSE_LIGHT replaces Godot's default diffuse, which allows banded (cel) shading.
smoothstep
0 below the first edge, 1 above the second, smooth between; narrow edges give crisp but not aliased bands.
ATTENUATION
The light's shadow and distance factor at the pixel; below 0.5 the pixel is treated as in shadow.
TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
Draws the material in the transparent pass, sorted back to front, so the fighter shows through the cactus or fern patch.
material_override
A material on the GeometryInstance3D that replaces the mesh's surface materials; the see-through swap changes only this property.
MultiMesh
Draws many copies of one mesh in one draw call with a transform (and optional colour) per instance; one per prop part keeps each part's outline.
set_meta / get_meta
Arbitrary values stored on an Object and saved in the scene; here the places and colours of each baked part.
SceneTree script (-s)
godot -s runs a script that extends SceneTree as the main loop; the bake uses it to load a scene, wait frames and save without the editor.
PackedScene.pack
Turns a node tree (nodes owned by the root) into a scene resource that ResourceSaver.save writes as .tscn.
GDScript as a value
A preloaded script is a resource whose constants and static functions can be called through a Variant; DrawnFighters.MODELS maps ids to such scripts.
start_unlocked()
The fighters every save has unlocked; SaveData adds them to older saves, so a new unlocked fighter reaches every player.
exclude_filter
Comma-separated globs of resource paths left out of the export pack; tools and tests are kept out the same way.
GUT
Godot Unit Test 9.7.1, the project's test framework; tools/test.ps1 runs every tests/test_*.gd headless.
